instructions: Stand on one leg. Explosively push off laterally, landing on the opposite leg in athletic stance. Stick the landing for 2s before rebounding. 5-6 per direction.
cues: knee tracks over toes on landing

name: Trap Bar Jump Squat
description: Loaded jump squat with a trap bar — joint-friendly version of a loaded jump, builds hip power with minimal spinal compression.
instructions: Stand in a trap bar holding the handles. Drop to a quarter squat and explode upward, leaving the floor if load allows. Land soft. Use 25-40% of trap bar deadlift max for load.
progression: Heavier load or banded trap bar jumps.

name: Neck CARs (Controlled Articular Rotations)
description: Slow, full-ROM neck circles under active control — recovery-level mobility for the neck after grappling or sparring.
instructions: Stand or sit tall. Slowly rotate the head through its full range of motion — flexion, side, extension, other side. Move at ~3-5s per quadrant. 3-5 rotations each direction.

name: Hip CARs
description: Single-leg hip rotation through full ROM — restores hip health in grapplers whose hips spend long periods in compressed ranges.
instructions: Stand tall next to a support. Lift one knee to hip height. Rotate the knee out to the side, extend the leg back, then return to start. Reverse. 3-5 per direction per leg.

name: Forearm Self-Massage (Grappler)
description: Targeted self-massage of forearm flexors/extensors — resolves post-gi or post-sparring forearm pump.
instructions: Sit and place one forearm on the opposite thigh. Use the heel of the other hand or a massage ball to work slowly up and down the forearm flexors and extensors. Spend 2-3 minutes per arm.
progression: Use a massage gun or lacrosse ball.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing Drill
description: Guided nasal diaphragmatic breathing — recovery and parasympathetic activation after hard rounds; also improves breath efficiency under submission pressure.
instructions: Lie supine with a hand on the chest, other on belly. Inhale through the nose slowly (4-5s), letting only the belly rise. Exhale through the mouth (6-8s). Repeat for 3-5 minutes.

name: Eccentric Wrist Extensor Curl
description: Slow eccentric wrist extensions — the evidence-based gold standard for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) rehab and prevention.
instructions: Sit with forearm supported on a bench, palm down, dumbbell in hand, wrist off the edge. Use the off-hand to assist lifting the weight to full wrist extension. Remove the assist and lower the wrist over 3-5 seconds to a hanging position. Reset and repeat. 15 reps per side.
home_variation: Light dumbbell or can of beans.
progression: Heavier dumbbell or Tyler Twist bar.

name: Eccentric Wrist Flexor Curl
description: Slow eccentric wrist flexion — medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow) rehab analogue.
instructions: Sit with forearm supported, palm up, dumbbell in hand, wrist off the bench edge. Use the off-hand to assist curling the wrist up, then lower slowly (3-5s) to full extension. Reset. 15 reps per side.

name: Isometric Wrist Extension Hold
description: Sustained isometric hold at the wrist — pain-modulation tool for acute tennis elbow flares.
instructions: Sit with forearm on a bench, palm down, hold a light dumbbell. Lift to ~30° wrist extension and hold for 30-45 seconds. Keep hold stationary. 4-5 reps per side with 30s rest.

name: Finger Rubber-Band Spreads
description: Individual-finger extension against a rubber band — targets extrinsic extensors often weak in racquet players.
instructions: Loop a rubber band around all five fingertips. Spread fingers apart against the band resistance, then slowly close. 25-40 reps per hand.
home_variation: Any elastic band or hair tie.

name: Forearm Pronation/Supination (Hammer)
description: Controlled forearm rotation with a weighted hammer — builds resilience in the racquet swing's finishing action.
instructions: Sit with forearm on bench, wrist off the edge, holding a hammer (or light dumbbell offset) by the end of the handle. Starting neutral, slowly rotate the palm to face up (supinate), then slowly face down (pronate). 10-12 reps per direction per side.

name: Radial Deviation with Hammer
description: Wrist radial deviation under load — trains the abductor pollicis / radial wrist muscles that stabilize during racquet contact.
instructions: Stand tall, hammer in hand hanging by the side with the head pointing forward. Lift the hammer head up by tilting the wrist toward the thumb side. Lower slowly. 10-12 reps per side.

name: Wrist Roller
description: Roll-up of a weight on a cord using wrist flexors and extensors — grip and forearm endurance for long racquet matches.
instructions: Hold a wrist roller (bar with a hanging weight on a cord) at arm's length. Roll the bar to wind the cord up, then reverse. 1-2 up/down cycles = one set.

name: Serratus Wall Slide
description: Wall slide emphasizing serratus anterior upward rotation — critical scapular control for overhead serve mechanics.
instructions: Stand facing a wall with forearms on the wall (elbows and wrists in contact). Press firmly into the wall so the shoulder blades wrap around the ribs. Slide arms up overhead while maintaining wall contact and serratus push. Return. 10-15 reps.
progression: Add a light foam roller between arms.

name: Prone T Raise
description: Prone horizontal abduction — isolated mid-trap and posterior-delt work to counter racquet-swing internal-rotation bias.
instructions: Lie face-down on a bench or floor, arms out to the sides in a T position with thumbs up. Squeeze the shoulder blades and lift arms off the floor to shoulder height. Pause. Lower slowly. 10-12 reps.

name: Bent-Over Reverse Fly
description: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly — direct posterior-delt and rhomboid load.
instructions: Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back, dumbbells hanging below shoulders. Lift both arms out to the sides to shoulder height while squeezing the shoulder blades. Pause, then lower. 10-15 reps.
progression: Heavier DBs or pause at top.

name: Overhead Band Pull-Apart
description: Band pull-apart performed overhead — trains lower trap and posterior cuff in the exact position the tennis serve loads.
instructions: Hold a light band overhead with arms straight, hands shoulder-width. Pull the band apart by driving the arms out to the sides while keeping them overhead. Return with control. 12-15 reps.
regression: Lighter band; arms in front not overhead.

name: Wall Scap Angel
description: Standing wall angel — combined scapular retraction and depression against gravity. A cleaner version of the floor snow angel.
instructions: Stand with back, glutes, and head against a wall. Arms up in a W position with backs of hands, wrists, and elbows touching the wall. Slowly slide arms up to Y, then back down to W without losing wall contact. 8-10 reps.
regression: Smaller ROM; arms never fully overhead.
progression: Hold a light band between hands.

name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
description: Kneeling T-spine rotation with hand on head — opens the thoracic spine for racquet swing follow-through.
instructions: On hands and knees, place one hand behind the head, elbow out. Rotate the elbow down under the body, then up toward the ceiling, leading with the elbow. Look where the elbow goes. 8 per side.
cues: rotate through the spine, not the hips

name: Landmine Rotational Press
description: Rotational landmine press — full kinetic chain, racquet-swing-specific loaded rotation.
instructions: Hold the end of a landmine bar at shoulder height with both hands, weight to one side. Rotate the hips and press the bar up and across the body to the opposite side. Return under control. 6-8 per side.
home_variation: Landmine or barbell in a corner.

name: Cable High-to-Low Chop
description: Cable chop from high to low across the body — mimics the downward-strike phase of the forehand and smash.
instructions: Set a cable pulley high. Stand sideways, grip the handle with both hands. Chop down and across the body to the opposite hip, rotating through the torso. Return with control. 10-12 per side.

name: Cable Low-to-High Lift
description: Cable lift from low to high across the body — mirrors the topspin forehand drive and open-stance strokes.
instructions: Set a cable pulley low. Stand sideways, grip the handle with both hands. Lift up and across the body to the opposite shoulder, rotating through the torso. Return with control. 10-12 per side.

name: Rotational Med-Ball Slam
description: Slam med ball downward and to the side — full-body rotational power with ground contact finish.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width, med ball overhead. Rotate to one side and slam the ball down hard next to the opposite foot. Catch the rebound (or pick up), rotate to the other side, slam. Alternate for reps.

name: Rotational Med-Ball Wall Pass
description: Side-facing med ball pass to a wall — pure rotational power with elastic return.
instructions: Stand 3-5 feet from a wall, sideways. Hold a med ball at the chest. Rotate explosively toward the wall and throw the ball at a chest-high target. Catch the rebound and repeat quickly. 8-10 per side.
cues: catch ready for the next rep

name: Split-Stance Explosive Press
description: Split-stance overhead med-ball push-press — single-leg base stability plus explosive overhead finish.
instructions: Stand in a split stance with a med ball at the chest. Dip the back knee slightly, then drive up through the front leg and press-throw the ball straight overhead. Catch or drop and reset. 5-6 per stance side.

name: Single-Leg Broad Jump (to Stick)
description: Unilateral horizontal jump with a stuck landing — builds confidence in single-leg force absorption (court deceleration).
instructions: Stand on one leg. Counter-movement into an explosive horizontal jump, landing on the SAME leg. Stick the landing with quiet foot and absorbed hip. Reset. 3-5 per side.
regression: Single-leg hop in place to stick.

name: Depth Drop to Stick
description: Step off a box and absorb the landing — dedicated deceleration training without the reactive jump-up of a depth jump.
instructions: Stand on a 12-18" box. Step off (don't jump). Land with both feet, immediately stick the landing: knees bent, hips back, chest up, quiet feet. Hold the landing 2-3 seconds. Step off and reset. 4-6 reps.

name: Reactive Lateral Shuffle with Cone
description: Partner- or cue-driven lateral shuffle between cones — court-reactive movement for pickleball/tennis dinking and pickup.
instructions: Set up two cones 6-10 feet apart. In athletic stance, shuffle toward whichever cone a partner points at or calls out. Change direction quickly on each call. 20-30 seconds per bout. Rest and repeat.
cues: change direction off the outside foot
eyes up — don't look at feet

name: Reaction Ball Catch
description: Drop and catch a reaction ball — pure hand-eye reactive training for racquet ball tracking.
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance holding a reaction ball at shoulder height. Drop it, let it bounce once, and catch it with one hand. Alternate hands. 20-30 catches per side.
home_variation: Reaction ball; tennis ball is an alternative.

name: Agility Ladder Icky Shuffle
description: Fast in-in-out ladder drill — footwork quickness and coordination for racquet court movement.
instructions: Set up an agility ladder. Step in-in-out pattern: left foot in, right foot in, left foot out to the side. Next square: right-left-right out. Move through the length of the ladder quickly. 3-4 passes.
cues: light on the balls of your feet

name: 5-10-5 Pro Agility Shuttle
description: Change-of-direction shuttle — gold standard test of COD for court sports.
instructions: Set three cones 5 yards apart in a line. Start at the middle cone. Sprint 5 yards to one side, touch the line, sprint 10 yards to the far cone, touch, sprint 5 yards back through the middle. 3-4 runs per direction.

name: Court Burst Interval
description: Short repeat sprints that mimic the 5-15 second rally bursts of racquet sports — energy-system specific conditioning.
instructions: On a court or open space, sprint hard for 10-15 seconds, then walk/rest for 30-45 seconds. Repeat for 8-12 bursts. Total work ~12-15 minutes.

name: Lateral Step-Down (Eccentric)
description: Slow eccentric lateral step-down — quad and glute-med control for sharp lateral court braking.
instructions: Stand on a 6-10" step on one foot, other leg hanging off the side. Slowly (3-4s) lower the hanging foot to the floor by flexing the standing hip and knee. Return to start. 8-10 per side.

name: Split-Stance Iso Hold
description: Wall-supported split-squat isometric hold — pre-event-safe knee and quad loading.
instructions: Set up in a split stance with the back foot elevated on a bench (or on the floor), torso upright, hands against a wall for support if desired. Lower to ~90° front knee. Hold 20-30 seconds. 3-4 holds per side.

name: Split-Stance Pallof Iso
description: Anti-rotation isometric in a split stance — bulletproof core for the racquet stroke anchor leg.
instructions: Set up a band or cable at chest height to the side. Step into a split stance facing perpendicular to the band. Hold the handle at the chest. Extend arms in front of you and hold 20-30 seconds, resisting the band's rotational pull. 3 holds per side per stance.

name: Sleeper Stretch Flow
description: Dynamic version of the posterior-capsule stretch — targets glenohumeral internal rotation deficit (GIRD) common in serve-dominant athletes.
instructions: Lie on one side, bottom shoulder under body, upper arm at 90° shoulder flexion, forearm vertical. Use the top hand to gently press the bottom forearm toward the floor for a 5-sec hold. Release. Repeat 8-10 times per side as a flow.

name: Hip 90/90 Breathing Flow
description: Seated 90/90 hip position with paced breathing — recovery mobility for the court-athlete hip.
instructions: Sit on the floor with one leg 90° in front (shin parallel to hips) and the other leg 90° to the side. Inhale 4s, exhale 6s. Hold 5-8 breaths. Rotate through the hips to swap sides (a "windshield wiper"). Continue 2-3 minutes.

name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
description: Foam roller T-spine extensions — reverses the flexed posture from long matches / desk work.
instructions: Lie supine with a foam roller across the mid-back. Hands behind the head or crossed over chest. Let the upper body arch back over the roller. Roll up 1-2" and repeat. 8-10 segments up the T-spine.

name: Forearm Trigger Point Release
description: Targeted self-myofascial release on the forearm flexors and extensors — essential recovery for the tennis-elbow-prone racquet player.
instructions: Using a lacrosse ball against a desk or wall (or a massage gun), press into the meat of the forearm. Slowly roll and pause on tight spots for 20-30 seconds. Cover both flexor (palm-side) and extensor (back-of-hand-side) compartments. 2-3 min per arm.

name: Wrist Circles + Finger Flicks
description: Combined warm-up flow: wrist circumduction + dynamic finger-extension flicks — fast warm-up for the hand and wrist before a match.
instructions: Hold arms in front. Make 10 slow wrist circles in each direction. Then: make a fist, flick all fingers open explosively. Repeat 15-20 times. Combine for a 2-minute warm-up.
cues: fingers spread wide on the flick

name: Ankle Rockers (Lateral)
description: Dynamic lateral ankle mobilization — ankle rockers in frontal plane for lateral court push-off.
instructions: Stand with feet wider than hips. Shift weight to one side, rocking the far-side foot onto the outer edge of the shoe while the near-side ankle dorsiflexes over the toes. Flow side-to-side. 10 per side.

name: Single-Arm Cable Paddle Pull
description: Standing single-arm cable row that mimics the catch-and-pull of a paddle stroke — primary dryland strength builder for paddlers.
instructions: Stand square to a mid-height cable with a single handle. From a staggered stance, reach the handle forward (catch), then pull past the hip with a rotating torso, driving the elbow back. Control the return. 8-12 reps per side.
cues: rotate the torso, don't just arm-pull
home_variation: Swim cords or resistance band anchored low.

name: Landmine Rotational Row
description: Bent-over row into the landmine with a rotational finish — trains the pull+rotate pattern under load.
instructions: Straddle a landmine barbell. Hinge at the hips, grab the bar sleeve with one hand. Row the bar toward the ribs while rotating the torso slightly open. Lower under control. Alternate sides or complete all reps one side first.
home_variation: DB single-arm row with slight rotation.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
description: Row performed prone on an incline bench — removes low-back involvement and isolates upper-back for pulling volume.
instructions: Lie chest-down on a 30-45° incline bench. Let dumbbells hang at arm's length. Row both dumbbells to the ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Lower under control.
home_variation: Single-arm DB row with bench support.

name: Renegade Row
description: Plank + alternating dumbbell row — anti-rotation core plus pulling strength, the exact demand of paddleboarding.
instructions: Start in a plank with hands on dumbbells, feet wide. Row one DB to the ribs while keeping hips square to the floor. Lower, switch sides. Avoid twisting the hips.
home_variation: Bodyweight plank rows on household objects.
progression: Heavier DBs or add push-up between rows.

name: Cable Low-to-High Chop
description: Diagonal rotational pull from low anchor to overhead — mimics the paddle catch lifting out of the water.
instructions: Anchor a cable low. Stand sideways to the stack, grip with both hands at hip. Pivot the back foot and drive the handle diagonally up and across to the opposite shoulder. Return slow and controlled.
home_variation: Band anchored to a low post.

name: Kneeling Pallof Press with Rotation
description: Tall-kneeling Pallof press that adds a small trunk rotation — bridge between anti-rotation and rotation for paddlers.
instructions: Tall-kneel perpendicular to a cable at chest height. Press the handle away from the chest; then slowly rotate the torso 20-30° toward the stack and back. Return the handle to the chest.
cues: rotate through the spine, not the hips
home_variation: Banded Pallof press with small rotation.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: Hanging knee/leg raise — strong core and grip endurance, directly transferable to paddling posture control.
instructions: Hang from a bar with a full grip. Without swinging, raise the legs (bent or straight depending on ability) to at least hip height. Lower slow.

name: Dragon Flag (Tuck)
description: Tucked dragon flag on a bench — advanced anti-extension core for surfers and SUP racers.
instructions: Lie on a bench, grip behind the head. Brace the core, lift the body off the bench in a tuck position (shoulders remain planted), then lower slowly controlling the hips.
regression: Hanging leg raise as progression lead-in.

name: Suspension Trainer Row (TRX)
description: Body-row variation with TRX — adjustable difficulty and portable, great traveling-surfer pull option.
instructions: Hold TRX handles; lean back with feet forward so arms are extended. Pull chest to handles, driving elbows back and squeezing the upper back. Lower with control.
cues: plank body from heels to head

name: Bent-Arm Bar Hang
description: Isometric pull-up hold — pulling endurance for long paddling sessions.
instructions: Pull up until the chin is over the bar and hold. Keep breathing. Drop when form breaks. 15-30 seconds.

name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Rotation
description: Half-kneeling rotational drive through the landmine — hip-driven rotation is the paddle stroke's engine.
instructions: Half-kneel perpendicular to the landmine. Hold the bar sleeve with both hands at one shoulder. Drive the bar across the body to the opposite shoulder by rotating through the torso. Return slow.
cues: rotate the torso, not the knees
home_variation: Cable rotational chop as equipment swap.

name: Rotational Med Ball Wall Throw
description: Rotational power throw into a wall — captures the paddle-drive and surf-turn moment without heavy CNS load.
instructions: Stand perpendicular to a wall, about 3 feet out. Rotate away from the wall, then drive through the hips to throw the ball into the wall with both hands. Catch and repeat.

name: Paddle Erg Intervals
description: Paddle ergometer interval training — the most sport-specific conditioning available indoors for paddlers.
instructions: Warm up 5 minutes. Perform 6-10 intervals of 60-90 seconds at 85-90% effort with equal rest. Cool down 5 minutes.
home_variation: Swim cords or cable pull circuit.
progression: Longer intervals or faster stroke rate.

name: Surfer Pop-Up Drill
description: Dryland pop-up — explosive prone-to-stance transition that is the foundational surf movement.
instructions: Lie prone on a mat as if on a board. From a push-up position, explosively pop both feet forward under the body, landing in a surf stance (front foot angled, knees bent). Reset to prone. Repeat.
progression: Pop-up with pause in bottom of push-up.

name: Prone Paddle on Stability Ball
description: Prone arm-stroke simulation on a stability ball — trains balance and paddle endurance for surfers.
instructions: Lie prone with the stability ball under the hips, feet lightly touching the floor or extended. Perform alternating arm strokes mimicking surf paddling. 30-60 seconds per bout.
cues: engage the core to avoid rolling

name: BOSU Single-Leg Balance
description: Balance on a BOSU (dome up) one-legged — builds the proprioceptive base for surfing, SUP, wakeboarding.
instructions: Step on the BOSU with one foot, soft bend in the knee. Hold balance 20-40 seconds. Progress to eyes closed or ball toss with a partner.
progression: Eyes closed or add upper-body motion.

name: Indo Board Balance Drill
description: Indo board rocking balance — surf/SUP-specific dynamic balance training.
instructions: Place feet shoulder-width on an indo board. Rock side-to-side or hold steady for 30-90 seconds. Progress to squats or catching a ball on the board.

name: Jump-Turn Pop-Up (180°)
description: Pop-up with a 180° rotation in mid-air — advanced surfer drill training landing in either stance.
instructions: Pop up explosively as in a standard pop-up, rotating 180° in the air to land facing the opposite direction in a surf stance. Absorb the landing.
cues: land soft in a low stance

name: Jefferson Curl
description: Loaded slow spinal flexion with a light weight — builds tissue resilience for the repeated flexion of prone paddling.
instructions: Stand tall on a box holding a light DB or kettlebell. Starting from the neck, slowly roll down vertebra by vertebra, letting the weight hang. Reverse slowly. Load light.
cues: only as deep as your mobility allows

name: Prone Cobra Hold
description: Prone cobra with arms in a low-Y — tonic endurance for the lumbar extensors that surfers rely on during paddling.
instructions: Lie prone, arms at sides with thumbs up. Lift the chest and arms off the floor, squeezing the mid-back. Hold for time.
progression: Longer hold or add light DBs.

name: Single-Leg RDL with Rotation
description: Single-leg RDL with a torso rotation at the bottom — hip-hinge balance and rotational stability for surfers/SUP.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a DB in the opposite hand. Hinge forward on the standing leg until the torso is parallel. At the bottom, rotate the torso slightly open. Return to standing.
progression: Heavier load or add pause at bottom.

name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat (Surf Stance)
description: Bulgarian split squat held in the surf stance — heavy quad/glute prep for the pop-up landing.
instructions: Place rear foot on a bench, front foot 2-3 feet ahead. Lower into a deep split squat, then drive up. Hold DBs for load.
progression: Heavier DBs or add a pause.

name: Drop-Knee Turn Simulation
description: Dryland drop-knee turn — trains the knee drop and lower leg drive used by surfers and longboarders in turns.
instructions: From a surf stance, drop the back knee low to the floor (over the back heel), then drive back up. Keep the front leg strong and bent.

name: Swim Cord Catch Pull
description: Single- or double-arm swim cord pulls from paddle-specific catch position — endurance for paddlers and surfers.
instructions: Anchor swim cords at chest height. Lean forward, arms extended overhead as at the catch. Pull cords past the hips with the torso engaged. Control the return.
home_variation: Swim cords or long resistance band.
progression: Heavier band or add faster tempo.

name: Kneeling Ski-Erg Pull
description: Tall-kneeling ski-erg pull — blends pulling power and core bracing for paddlers.
instructions: Tall-kneel in front of a ski erg. Pull the handles from overhead down to the hips with a full torso engagement. Reset overhead with control.
progression: Longer bouts or kneel on unstable surface.

name: Prone Y Raise on Incline
description: Prone Y raise from an incline bench — targets lower traps for posterior-shoulder endurance critical to paddlers and surfers.
instructions: Lie chest-down on a 30° incline bench. With light DBs, raise arms overhead in a Y shape with thumbs up. Hold 1 sec. Lower slow.

name: Scapular Wall Slide
description: Wall slide — scap upward-rotation drill and shoulder flexion mobility for paddlers.
instructions: Stand with back against a wall, arms in goalpost position. Slowly slide the arms overhead, keeping the forearms and low back in contact with the wall. Return.
progression: Add a band between the wrists.

name: Serratus Wall Push-Up
description: Plus-rep push-up at a wall — activates serratus anterior for scap stability during paddling.
instructions: Stand facing a wall in a push-up position. From a normal push-up top, press the shoulder blades further apart (protract). Control the return. 10-15 reps.

name: Banded 90-90 External Rotation
description: Shoulder external rotation at 90° abduction — critical rotator-cuff strength for paddling overhead reach.
instructions: Stand sideways to a band anchored at shoulder height. Elbow bent 90°, upper arm parallel to floor. Rotate the forearm up against band resistance. Lower slow.

name: Shoulder Distraction Hang
description: Passive hang for shoulder decompression — the single best recovery tool for paddle-sore shoulders.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with relaxed shoulders (let the shoulders shrug up). Breathe. 20-45 seconds per hang.

name: Thread-the-Needle Reach
description: T-spine rotation drill with an active reach — opens the mid-back rotation paddlers lose over time.
instructions: Quadruped position. Thread one arm under the opposite chest, then reach the threaded arm out to the side and up toward the ceiling, opening the chest. Return. Alternate.
progression: Add a DB for load in reach-up arm.

name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
description: Thoracic rotation from a quadruped position — active t-spine mobility for rotational paddlers.
instructions: Quadruped, one hand behind head. Rotate the elbow down toward the opposite wrist, then open up toward the ceiling. 8-10 per side.
progression: Add a light reach-across with DB.

name: Bretzel Stretch
description: Side-lying combined hip-flexor and t-spine rotation stretch — addresses paddler posture in one move.
instructions: Lie on one side, bottom leg straight, top leg bent with foot anchored in opposite hand. Other hand grabs the top knee. Rotate the upper torso open, looking over the shoulder. Hold 30-45 seconds. Switch.

name: Cat-Cow Extension Hold
description: Active spinal extension hold at the top of cat-cow — counteracts prone-paddling flexion loads.
instructions: From a quadruped cat-cow, move into full extension (head up, belly down) and hold 3-5 seconds. Breathe. Return to neutral. Repeat.

name: Ski-Erg Intervals
description: Ski-erg intervals — upper-body pulling conditioning that crosses over strongly to paddling.
instructions: Warm up 5 minutes. Perform 5-8 intervals of 60 seconds at 85% effort, 60 seconds rest. Cool down 5 minutes.

name: Long Steady Paddle-Erg (Zone 2)
description: Extended zone-2 paddling — aerobic base for open-water paddlers and distance rowers.
instructions: Paddle erg 30-60 minutes at conversational pace (Zone 2, 60-70% max HR). Keep stroke rate even.
progression: Longer duration or add tempo pickups.

name: Rower + Push-Up EMOM
description: EMOM (every minute on the minute) mixing rowing erg calories with push-ups — conditioning + antagonist balance.
instructions: Set a 10-20 minute EMOM. Alternate minutes: minute 1 — 15-20 cal row; minute 2 — 12-15 push-ups. Rest the remainder of each minute.

name: Tabata Paddle Pull
description: 4-minute tabata on the paddle erg or swim cords — high-intensity pulling for short-course paddlers.
instructions: 8 rounds: 20 seconds max effort paddle pull, 10 seconds rest. 4 minutes total work.

name: Kneeling Upright Row Endurance
description: Kneeling high-rep kettlebell or DB upright row — shoulder and trap endurance for long paddling days.
instructions: Tall-kneel with a KB in one or both hands. Pull the weight up to the collarbone leading with the elbows. 20-30 reps continuous.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Chop (High-to-Low)
description: Diagonal chop from high to low in a half-kneeling stance — core + hip stability for paddlers and surfers.
instructions: Half-kneel perpendicular to a cable anchored high. Grip the handle with both hands at the high-side shoulder. Chop diagonally down and across toward the opposite hip. Control the return.

name: Cossack Lunge with Reach
description: Cossack squat adding a same-side arm reach overhead — lateral hip mobility with thoracic rotation for surfers.
instructions: Drop into a cossack squat on one side. At the bottom, reach the bent-side arm overhead and laterally open. Stand up and alternate sides.
progression: Add a DB in reach arm.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust on Bench
description: Single-leg hip thrust — glute strength critical for pop-up drive and stance stability.
instructions: Upper back on a bench, feet on floor. Extend one leg straight. Drive through the planted heel to lift the hips to full extension. Lower slow.
cues: squeeze the glute at the top

name: Standing Single-Arm Landmine Row
description: Standing landmine row, one arm at a time — core anti-rotation + pulling strength for paddlers.
instructions: Stand beside a landmine. Hinge, grip the sleeve with one hand. Row the bar to the ribs without rotating the torso. Lower slow.
cues: row to the ribs, not to the shoulder

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
description: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch — essential recovery move for kayakers and rowers who sit flexed for hours.
instructions: Half-kneel, back foot on mat. Tuck the pelvis slightly, drive the hips forward until a stretch is felt in the front of the rear hip. Hold 30-45 seconds per side.

name: Foam Roll Lats
description: Self-myofascial release of the lats — top recovery tool for paddlers with chronically loaded lats.
instructions: Lie on one side with the foam roller under the armpit. Extend the arm long overhead. Roll slowly from armpit down to ribcage. 60-90 seconds per side.

name: Sleeper Stretch
description: Side-lying shoulder internal rotation stretch — opens the posterior capsule that paddlers chronically tighten.
instructions: Lie on one side, bottom shoulder and arm bent 90°. With the top hand, gently press the bottom forearm toward the floor. Hold 30-45 seconds. Switch sides.

name: Reverse Nordic Curl
description: Kneeling quad-eccentric — builds the rectus femoris length-under-load that sprinters and soccer players need to avoid hip-flexor and quad strains.
instructions: Kneel with knees hip-width apart, feet pointed. Keep the body rigid from knees to head. Slowly lean backward by extending the hips, reaching as far back as quads allow. Return to upright with control.
progression: Add a load (plate at chest) or deeper lean.

name: Banded Adductor Pulldown (Standing)
description: Standing hip-adduction against a band — targets the adductor complex for cutting and kicking sports.
instructions: Loop a band around one ankle with the anchor at hip height to the side. Stand tall with weight on the non-banded leg. Pull the banded leg across the body midline, squeezing adductors. Return slowly.
progression: Heavier band or add pause at end range.

name: Lateral Deceleration Drill
description: Sprint-and-stop footwork drill — teaches safe lateral deceleration, the most common ACL-injury mechanism in soccer and basketball.
instructions: Set two cones 8-10 yards apart. Accelerate laterally toward one cone, then decelerate into a wide athletic stance (hips back, knees bent, chest up). Hold for a 1-count. Reset and repeat.
home_variation: Two cones or markers on any field.
regression: Slower walkthrough of the stop position.
progression: Add a partner cue or reactive direction change.

name: Single-Leg Land Mechanics (Drop-Stick)
description: Controlled unilateral landing from a low box — reprograms clean single-leg landing, critical for basketball, volleyball, and soccer jumpers.
instructions: Stand on a 6-12" box on one leg. Step off (do not jump) and land on the same leg. "Stick" the landing — hips back, knee tracks over the middle toe, hold for 2 seconds. Return to box via the opposite leg.
cues: knee over middle toe — no inward collapse
progression: Higher box, reactive cue on landing.

name: Volleyball Approach Jump
description: Three-step spike approach into a max vertical — sport-specific plyo for volleyball hitters.
instructions: Set a target overhead (wall mark or net). From 3-4 steps out, take the classic 3-step approach (L-R-L for right-handers), plant both feet, swing arms, and jump as high as possible. Reach with the hitting arm. Land soft and reset.

name: Banded ACL Prehab — Terminal Knee Extension
description: Banded terminal-knee-extension — foundational VMO activation and ACL-support drill.
instructions: Loop a band around a sturdy post at knee height and behind one knee. Stand facing the anchor with slight knee bend. Extend the knee fully against band resistance, squeezing the quad at lockout. Return with control.
progression: Heavier band or isometric hold at end range.

name: Ankle CARs (Controlled Articular Rotations)
description: Active ankle mobility sweep in every direction — builds full ROM and joint resilience, key for ankle-injury-heavy sports.
instructions: Seated or supine, extend one leg. Slowly draw the largest possible circle with the foot, moving through dorsiflexion, inversion, plantarflexion, and eversion. Keep the knee still. 5 per direction per side.
cues: isolate the ankle — knee stays still

name: Prone Y-T-W-L Complex
description: Lower-trap + rotator-cuff complex — four-position posterior-shoulder builder, the workhorse for overhead sports.
instructions: Lie face-down on a bench or floor. In sequence: arms overhead Y, out to sides T, elbows bent W, then L (90°elbow, rotate up). 8-10 of each, moving continuously.
progression: Light DBs (1-3 lb) or slower tempo.

name: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation (Banded)
description: Isometric band-held external rotation — builds the cuff-strength endurance baseball and cricket throwers rely on.
instructions: Stand with elbow tucked at 90°. Hold a band pulled across the body, light tension. Resist the band (do not move) for a 20-30s hold. Switch arms.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Lift
description: Anti-rotation lift in half-kneeling — builds the diagonal chain (hip to opposite shoulder) used in throwing and batting.
instructions: Half-kneel with the outside knee down, cable anchored low to that side. Grip the handle with both hands. Lift the handle diagonally across the body up to overhead on the opposite side. Control the return.
cues: initiate from the core, not arms
progression: Heavier load or standing cable chop variant.

name: Rotational Scoop Toss (Med Ball)
description: Low-to-high rotational throw — baseball/softball hitting power and hockey slap-shot mechanics.
instructions: Stand sideways to a wall with feet wider than shoulders. Hold a med ball at hip height on the outside hip. Rotate through the trail hip and scoop/throw the ball upward and into the wall. Catch rebound and reset.

name: Med Ball Chest Pass (Explosive)
description: Horizontal chest pass for explosive upper-body push — basketball outlet pass and football pushing power.
instructions: Stand 6-10 feet from a wall. Hold a med ball at the chest. Explosively push the ball into the wall with both hands, extending fully. Catch the rebound and repeat without pause.
progression: Heavier ball or single-arm shot-put variant.

name: Single-Leg Lateral Bound to Stick
description: Unilateral lateral hop with stuck landing — hockey stride power and lateral cutting athleticism.
instructions: Stand on one leg. Explosively hop sideways as far as possible onto the opposite leg. Stick the landing for a 2-count. Reset and hop back.

name: Hip Airplane
description: Standing single-leg rotational balance — bulletproofs hip stability for pitchers, cutters, and runners.
instructions: Stand on one leg, hinge forward at the hip until torso is parallel to the floor, free leg extended behind. Rotate the lifted hip open (external rotation), then closed (internal rotation). Continuous flow.
home_variation: Bodyweight; touch a wall for balance.
regression: Hold onto a wall or pole.

name: Nordic Curl (Assisted/Regression)
description: Band-assisted Nordic curl — teaches the eccentric hamstring pattern safely for those not yet strong enough for a full Nordic.
instructions: Kneel with ankles anchored, band looped around the chest and to a sturdy point overhead/forward for assist. Slowly lower forward, using band to control the last portion. Push back up with hands if needed.
cues: drive through the hamstrings as long as possible
home_variation: Band + sturdy anchor + partner or furniture for ankles.
progression: Less band assistance — progress to unassisted Nordic (102).

name: Long-Toss Warm-Up Progression
description: Throwing-distance progression drill — the arm-care staple used by baseball and softball players to prep the shoulder for competition.
instructions: Start with easy 15-ft tosses (20 throws), progress to 45 ft (15 throws), 60 ft (10 throws), 90+ ft (5-8 throws). Focus on crow-hop mechanics and clean arm action. Scale distances to available space.
regression: Stop at 45 ft for younger/older arms.
progression: Add pulldowns or max-effort long toss.

name: 5-10-5 Pro Agility Shuttle
description: Short-distance shuttle — the NFL/NBA combine staple. Tests and trains change-of-direction speed in every team sport.
instructions: Set three cones in a line, 5 yards apart. Straddle the middle cone. Sprint 5 yards one way, touch the line, sprint 10 yards the other way, touch, sprint back through the middle. Rest fully.
cues: touch the line with the hand

name: Shuttle Run Conditioning (Suicides)
description: Court/field shuttle conditioning — the standard team-sport anaerobic-capacity builder.
instructions: Set cones at 10, 20, 30, and 40 yards from the start. Sprint to first cone and back, second cone and back, and so on. Rest equal to work. 3-5 rounds.

name: Yo-Yo Intermittent Intervals
description: Intermittent shuttle test-style conditioning — soccer/rugby/hockey-specific repeated-sprint capacity.
instructions: Mark 20m shuttle. Run out, touch, return — then 10s recovery jog/walk. Repeat at target pace (~12-18 km/h progressing). 15-25 intervals.

name: Tempo Run (100m)
description: Sub-max 70-80% tempo runs — aerobic capacity and recovery between sessions for field-sport athletes.
instructions: On a track or open field, run 100m at roughly 70-80% max. Walk back. Repeat 8-12 times. Focus on smooth mechanics — not max speed.

name: Spider-Man Walk
description: Walking lunge with T-spine rotation — full-body warm-up essential for team-sport athletes.
instructions: From standing, step into a deep lunge. Place the same-side hand inside the lead foot. Rotate the opposite hand up to the sky. Return hand, step back, and repeat on the other side. 5-8 per side.

name: Foam Roll IT Band
description: Lateral thigh self-myofascial work — addresses the IT band / TFL tightness common in runners and cutters.
instructions: Lie on side with foam roller under the outer thigh. Slowly roll from hip to just above knee. Pause 10-20 sec on any tender spot. Work for 60-90 sec per side.
cues: avoid rolling directly over the knee
progression: Use a lacrosse ball for more pressure.

name: Foam Roll Adductors
description: Inner-thigh self-myofascial work — adductor recovery for groin-heavy sports (soccer, hockey, rugby).
instructions: Lie face-down with one leg out to the side, foam roller under the adductor. Slowly roll from groin to knee. Work tender spots for 60-90 sec per side.
progression: Lacrosse ball for more pinpoint pressure.

name: Box Breathing 4-4-4-4
description: Parasympathetic breathwork — 4-4-4-4 box pattern for post-game recovery and stress management.
instructions: Seated or supine. Inhale through nose for 4 counts. Hold 4 counts. Exhale through nose/mouth for 4 counts. Hold empty 4 counts. Repeat for 3-5 minutes.

name: Thoracic Extension on Foam Roller
description: Supine foam-roller thoracic extension — reopens the upper back for overhead athletes and desk-bound rec-leaguers.
instructions: Lie supine with foam roller across the mid-back (bra-line). Hands support the head. Slowly extend back over the roller. Move the roller 1-2 inches up or down and repeat. Cover mid-thoracic segments.
cues: don't extend at the low back
regression: Towel roll instead of foam roller.

name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Band Mobilization
description: Band-distracted ankle dorsiflexion — restores dorsiflexion critical for squatting, cutting, and landing.
instructions: Anchor a heavy band low and loop it around the front of the ankle. Half-kneel with the banded ankle forward, band pulling the tibia back. Drive the knee forward over the toes, holding 2-3 sec. 10-15 per side.
cues: feel stretch in the front of the ankle
progression: Add a small plate under the toes.

name: Pigeon Pose
description: Deep external-rotation hip stretch — releases piriformis and glute-med tightness that contributes to low-back and knee issues.
instructions: From plank, bring one knee forward toward the same-side wrist, shin angled across. Extend the back leg straight behind. Lower chest toward the floor over the forward shin. Hold 60-90 sec per side.
cues: don't force — breathe into the stretch
no sharp knee pain — back off if pinching
progression: Extended forward fold over the shin.

name: Couch Stretch Active (Hip Flexor)
description: Active hip-flexor lengthening with glute drive — unlocks the hip flexors shortened by sitting and sprinting.
instructions: Kneel with one foot elevated behind on a couch/bench, shin vertical. Torso upright. Actively squeeze the glute of the rear leg while tucking the pelvis. Hold 30-45 sec, release, repeat.

name: Groin Stretch Active (Frog Rock)
description: Quadruped adductor mobilization — restores adductor range for soccer, hockey, and grappling athletes.
instructions: Quadruped with knees wide, toes flexed. Rock hips back toward the heels until a firm stretch. Rock forward slightly and repeat. 8-12 rocks.
progression: Wider stance and longer hold at each rock.

name: Front Squat (Barbell)
description: Upright-torso barbell squat with front-rack load — quad-dominant strength that preserves a tall posture valuable for athletes.
instructions: Set the bar in a front rack (elbows high). Step back from the rack. Descend to at least parallel with knees tracking over toes. Stand tall. Reset.
cues: chest tall all the way down
progression: Heavier front squat or tempo pause.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
description: Hex-bar deadlift — athlete-friendly deadlift variation that hits quads and posterior chain without the spinal demand of a barbell pull.
instructions: Stand inside a hex bar. Hinge and grip handles. Set a neutral spine, drive through floor to stand tall. Lower under control.
progression: Heavier trap bar or paused deadlift.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
description: Horizontal shoulder abduction with dumbbells — posterior deltoid and mid-trap strength for posture and antagonist balance.
instructions: Hinge at hips with dumbbells hanging. Keeping slight elbow bend, raise DBs out to the sides until arms parallel to floor. Lower with control.

name: Face Pull with External Rotation
description: Face pull finished with external rotation — the posterior-shoulder and rotator-cuff combo for overhead-sport athletes.
instructions: Cable/band at face height. Pull the rope toward the face while externally rotating the forearms up (ending in a W position). Reverse under control.

name: Neck Isometric 4-Way
description: Four-direction isometric neck holds — builds cervical strength for rugby, lacrosse, and collision sports.
instructions: Seated or standing. Place hand on forehead, resist as you push head forward (30 sec). Switch to back of head (push back). Then sides (push laterally). All sub-max, no head movement.

name: Banded Neck Lateral Flexion
description: Resisted neck lateral flexion — targeted cervical strengthening for contact-sport athletes.
instructions: Loop a band around the head (over the ear) anchored to the side. Lateral-flex the head away from the anchor against band resistance. Return with control.

name: Cable External Rotation at 90° (Sleeper)
description: Shoulder external rotation at 90° abduction — the throwing-position cuff-strength exercise used by baseball arm-care programs.
instructions: Set cable/band at elbow height. Stand with banded arm abducted 90° (elbow at shoulder height, forearm parallel to floor). Rotate the forearm up and back. Return under control.
home_variation: Cable or band at elbow height.

name: Banded Hip-Flexor Antagonist March
description: Supine band-resisted march — hip-flexor strength in a neutral pelvis; counteracts chronic adductor/quad dominance in team-sport athletes.
instructions: Supine with a band looped around both feet, anchored low. Press low back into floor. Bring one knee to 90°, resist on the way back. Alternate legs.
progression: Heavier band or add torso flex.

name: Single-Arm Landmine Row
description: Single-arm row with a landmine — anti-rotation loaded pull, the team-sport core-and-back combo.
instructions: Set a barbell in a landmine. Straddle the sleeve facing away. Hinge and grip the sleeve in one hand. Row the barbell up while resisting torso rotation. Lower under control.

name: Glute Medius Side Plank Clamshell
description: Side plank with top-leg clamshell — combined lateral core and glute-med endurance.
instructions: Forearm side plank, stacked feet. While holding the plank, open the top knee (clamshell) while keeping feet together. Control the return. 8-10 reps per side.

name: Copenhagen Hold Short Lever
description: Short-lever Copenhagen plank — regression to the full Copenhagen that progressively loads adductors.
instructions: Side plank on forearm with the top knee (not foot) on a bench. Lift the bottom hip off the floor, squeezing the adductor. Hold 15-30 sec per side.
progression: Progress to long-lever Copenhagen (106) or dynamic (237).

name: Standing Hip Abduction (Banded)
description: Standing banded hip abduction — functional glute-med loading in a sport-relevant upright posture.
instructions: Band around ankles, stand on one leg. Abduct the free leg out to the side against band resistance. Control the return. 12-15 per side.
progression: Heavier band or pause at top.

name: Reaction Ball Drop and Catch
description: Proprioception drill with a reaction ball — builds the first-step quickness and hand reactivity for all team sports.
instructions: Hold reaction ball at shoulder height. Drop it, let it bounce once, catch it on the unpredictable rebound. 30-60 sec continuous work per set.

name: Cone Cutting Drill (T-Drill)
description: Four-cone T-shape cutting drill — multi-planar agility combining forward sprint, lateral shuffle, and backpedal.
instructions: Set cones in a T (top bar 10 yards, stem 10 yards). Sprint stem to middle cone, shuffle right to end cone, shuffle across to opposite cone, shuffle back to middle, backpedal to start.
cues: don't cross feet on the shuffle

name: Agility Ladder In-Out
description: Agility-ladder footwork drill — fast-feet training for basketball, soccer, and hockey footwork.
instructions: With an agility ladder flat on ground, move through with the in-in-out-out pattern (both feet in each square, then both feet out straddling). Work length of ladder, reset.

name: Slide Board Lateral
description: Slide-board lateral push-offs — off-ice specific training for hockey and lateral deceleration for all team sports.
instructions: Stand on a slide board with booties. Push off one end with the inside foot, glide to the other side, and absorb with the outside leg. Continuous sliding for 30-60 sec per set.
regression: Lateral shuffle on a smooth floor.

name: Dot Drill (5-Dot)
description: Five-dot reactive footwork drill — foot-speed, quickness, and coordination for all team sports.
instructions: Tape 5 dots in an X pattern (four corners + center, ~18" apart). Hop through patterns (front-back, side-side, scissor) for 10-15 sec per round.

name: Rope Skip (Speed Rope)
description: Speed jump rope — calf and ankle reactive conditioning, cheap and travel-friendly for any team-sport athlete.
instructions: With a speed rope, skip for 30-60 sec rounds. Stay on the balls of the feet, small hops, fast rope tempo. 3-5 rounds.
regression: Shorter rounds or no rope (ghost rope).

name: Drop to Vertical Jump
description: Step-off from a box immediately into a max vertical jump — reactive-strength primer before full depth jumps.
instructions: Stand on a 6-12" box. Step off. On landing, immediately jump vertically for max height. Aim to minimize ground-contact time.

name: Peroneal Band Eversion
description: Peroneal strengthening — direct prehab for lateral ankle sprains that plague skateboarders and dancers.
instructions: Sit with legs extended. Loop a mini-band around the outside of one foot, anchor the other end (chair leg or other foot). Pull the foot outward (eversion) against the band. 15-20 reps per side.

name: Slide-Board Lateral Skate
description: Slide-board push — speciality skating-stride prep; builds lateral hip power and glide endurance.
instructions: Stand on a slide board with booties. Push off one foot to glide laterally to the opposite bumper, catching weight on the other foot. Continue side-to-side for 30-60 seconds.
cues: arms swing like a speed skater
home_variation: Socks on a hardwood floor with towels.

name: Lateral Bound to Stick
description: Single-leg lateral hop with stuck landing — skating-specific power and landing control.
instructions: Stand on one leg. Push off laterally and leap sideways as far as possible, landing on the opposite leg. Hold the landing for 2 seconds before the next rep.
cues: push hard from the outside edge

name: Slackline Walk
description: Dynamic full-body balance on a moving line — proprioceptive dynamite for any wheeled sport.
instructions: Anchor a slackline 12-18 inches off the ground between two trees/posts. Step on, find balance, and walk. Arms out for balance. Fall safely.
progression: Walking backward or turning on the line.

name: Skater's Step-Down (Eccentric)
description: Slow eccentric step-down emphasizing knee control during deceleration — protects skater knees.
instructions: Stand on one leg on a 6-12" box. Over 3-4 seconds, slowly lower the other leg to tap the floor, controlling with the standing leg. Return to standing.

name: Push-Up Plyo (Wrist Fall Prep)
description: Reactive push-up — builds upper-body shock tolerance for the inevitable skater fall.
instructions: From a push-up position, explosively push off the floor so hands leave briefly. Land softly with slightly bent elbows and repeat. Progress to clap push-ups.
progression: Clap push-up or deficit plyo push-up.

name: Wrist Push-Up (Front)
description: Wrist-strengthening push-up variant that loads wrist flexors through extension — essential fall tolerance.
instructions: In quadruped or push-up position, place hands flat with fingers pointing forward. Slowly shift weight forward and back, progressively loading the extended wrist. Start on knees.

name: Hip 90/90 with Transitions
description: Dynamic 90/90 hip flows — hip rotator mobility for skaters, dancers, yogis.
instructions: Sit with one leg bent 90° in front, the other 90° to the side. Lift both knees and rotate to the opposite side. Flow back and forth for 8-10 reps per side.

name: Standing Hip External Rotation (Banded)
description: Banded standing external rotation — glute-med in standing position for carving skaters.
instructions: Loop a mini-band above the knees. Stand on one leg with the other knee lifted to 90°. Rotate the lifted knee outward against the band without tipping the pelvis.
progression: Standing with added ankle band load.

name: Deceleration Skater Hold
description: Landing-position isometric — trains skaters to absorb and hold a deep lateral stance.
instructions: From standing, hop laterally onto one leg and hold the landing in a quarter-squat with the other leg trailing behind (skater pose). Hold 3-5 seconds, then reset.
progression: Hop + deeper hold or added reach.

name: Tib Raise on Step
description: Elevated tibialis raise — shin-strength insurance for skaters and parkour landings.
instructions: Stand with heels on the edge of a step, toes lifted. Slowly lift toes up and then lower them below parallel for a stretched tibialis. 15-20 reps.

name: Weighted Carve Squat
description: Rotational squat with torso rotation — mimics pumping/carving on a skateboard/surfboard.
instructions: Hold a light DB or plate at chest. Squat to parallel while rotating the torso toward one knee. Stand and rotate to the other knee on the next rep.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: Gymnastics-standard core hold — full-body compression essential for handstands and levers.
instructions: Lie supine. Press low back into the floor. Lift shoulders and straight legs 4-6 inches off the floor. Arms overhead. Hold 20-45 seconds.
regression: Tuck hollow or hands at sides.

name: Arch Body Hold (Reverse Hollow)
description: Posterior-chain counterpart to the hollow — trains the front-lever and back-line extension gymnasts need.
instructions: Lie prone. Arms overhead. Lift arms, chest, and legs simultaneously into a reverse banana. Squeeze glutes. Hold 20-45 seconds.

name: Tuck L-Sit Progression
description: L-sit foundation — hip-flexor and core compression for calisthenics.
instructions: Sit on the floor or parallettes with hands planted. Depress shoulders and lift both knees tucked toward the chest, hips off the floor. Hold 10-20 seconds.
regression: Support on blocks; feet on the floor.

name: Planche Lean
description: Straight-arm anterior shoulder loading — the primary planche progression.
instructions: In plank, lock elbows straight and protract scaps. Shift shoulders forward past the wrists as far as comfortable. Hold 10-20 seconds.

name: Handstand Wall Hold
description: Wall-supported handstand — foundational inversion for gymnasts, yogis, calisthenics athletes.
instructions: Kick up to a handstand with the belly facing a wall or back against a wall. Stack shoulders over wrists. Hold 20-45 seconds. Focus on active shoulders and stacked body.

name: Ring Dip (False Grip Optional)
description: Gymnastics-ring dip — essential pushing strength for muscle-up and ring work.
instructions: Hang at the top of rings with straight arms, rings turned out. Lower the body until shoulders are just below the rings. Press back up with control.

name: Muscle-Up Transition Drill
description: Chest-to-bar high pull + transition — specific drill for the calisthenics muscle-up.
instructions: From a dead hang, perform an explosive pull that brings the chest above the bar. At the peak, drive elbows back and transition over the bar into a dip support.
cues: turn the elbows at the top

name: Parkour Precision Jump to Line
description: Two-foot jump to stick — parkour's foundational landing accuracy drill.
instructions: Mark a target line ~1-1.5m away. From two feet, jump and stick the landing on the line with both feet hitting simultaneously. Hold for 2 seconds. Reset and repeat.
progression: Jump to a raised rail or narrow target.

name: Depth Landing (No Rebound)
description: Drop from height and absorb silently — landing mechanics for parkour and gymnastics.
instructions: Step off a 12-24 inch box (do not jump). Absorb the landing with quiet feet, knees tracking toes, and hips back. Stick the landing completely silently.

name: Quadrupedal Crawl (QM)
description: Low crawl with contralateral hand/foot movement — fundamental parkour + movement-culture pattern.
instructions: Start on hands and feet (not knees), hips low. Crawl forward moving opposite hand and opposite foot together. Maintain low hips and quiet feet.

name: Vault Kong Progression
description: Entry parkour vault pattern over a low obstacle — builds shoulder push + hip compression.
instructions: Run up to a waist-high object. Place both hands on top, tuck knees to chest between the hands, and pass both legs through to land on the far side.
progression: Full kong vault over taller obstacle.

name: Hollow-to-Arch Rock
description: Transition between hollow and arch — gymnastics warm-up staple.
instructions: Start in hollow body. Roll to prone and into arch body position. Roll back to hollow. Maintain tension throughout each position.

name: Jefferson Curl Standing (Unloaded)
description: Unloaded spinal roll-down — gentle segmental flexion for yoga and dance warm-ups.
instructions: Stand tall. Tuck chin and slowly roll down one vertebra at a time. Let arms hang. Reverse the roll slowly from the tailbone up.

name: Body Row (Rings or Bar)
description: Inverted row on rings — horizontal pull strength that scales endlessly for pole and calisthenics.
instructions: Hang under a set of rings or a bar with straight body, heels on the floor. Pull chest to the rings, retracting scaps first. Lower with control.

name: Pike Compression Lift
description: Seated pike leg lift — compression strength for L-sits, V-sits, and pole inverts.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended in a pike. Hands flat next to hips. Lift straight legs as high as possible while keeping a pike position. Hold 1-2 seconds, lower.

name: Thread-the-Needle (Yoga)
description: Thoracic rotation stretch from quadruped — staple yoga/movement thoracic opener.
instructions: From tabletop, thread one arm under the other, lowering shoulder and temple to the floor. Hold 30-45 seconds. Switch sides.
progression: Add arm reach for deeper stretch.

name: Pilates Hundred
description: Classical Pilates core primer — sustained core activation with breath coordination.
instructions: Lie supine. Lift head and shoulders, extend legs to a tabletop or low hover. Arms hover palms down beside hips. Pulse arms 100 times while inhaling for 5 and exhaling for 5.

name: Yogi Push-Up (Chaturanga)
description: Yoga-specific tricep push-up with elbows tight — key repeated pattern in vinyasa practice.
instructions: From plank, shift slightly forward. Lower slowly keeping elbows tight to the body until upper arms are parallel to the floor. Pause, then flow to up-dog or push back up.

name: Wall Walk (Handstand Approach)
description: Walk the feet up a wall into handstand position — builds inversion confidence and shoulder endurance.
instructions: Start in push-up facing away from wall. Walk feet up the wall while hands walk toward the wall until reaching handstand. Reverse.

name: Standing Splits Prep (Dancer's Splits)
description: Active standing split progression — hamstring/hip-flexor mobility for dancers and martial artists.
instructions: Stand on one leg. Lift the free leg forward/up as high as possible actively (no hands). Hold 5-10 seconds. Lower. Repeat to the side and then back.

name: Cat-Cow Flow (Slow)
description: Slow segmental spinal flexion/extension — daily spinal health flow for yogis and desk workers.
instructions: Tabletop. Inhale: drop belly, lift chest and tail (cow). Exhale: round spine, tuck tail, drop head (cat). Move one vertebra at a time.

name: Wall Sit Variation with Heel Lift
description: Wall sit with alternating heel lifts — quad endurance + calf activation for dancers and ballet.
instructions: Wall sit at 90° knee. Alternately lift one heel at a time (as in relevé) while holding the sit. Continue for 30-60 seconds.
progression: Higher wall sit with longer holds.

name: Pole/Bar Invert Tuck
description: Pole-fitness invert tuck progression — grip + compression to invert.
instructions: Grip the pole/bar with both hands. Pull up while tucking knees to chest. Roll hips back to inverted position, legs tucked. Lower with control.

name: Shoulder Flossing with Band
description: Banded shoulder dislocates with isolation — shoulder joint health for gymnasts and yogis.
instructions: Hold a light band wide overhead. Rotate arms slowly from front to overhead to behind the body, then reverse. Keep arms straight. 8-10 cycles.

name: Relevé Calf Raise (Ballet)
description: Ballet-style relevé — full-range calf raise onto the balls of the feet, key for all dance forms.
instructions: Stand tall, heels together in first position (or parallel). Rise onto the balls of the feet as high as possible while staying tall. Lower with control.
cues: rise to the ball of the big toe

name: Single-Leg Relevé with Balance
description: Unilateral relevé held on one leg — balance + calf strength for pointe work and turns.
instructions: Stand on one leg. Rise onto the ball of the foot and hold 5-10 seconds. Lower with control. Switch sides.

name: Turn-Prep Pirouette Drill
description: Pirouette passé prep — stand on single leg in relevé with the other foot at the knee.
instructions: Start in fourth position. Brush the working leg up to passé while rising onto the supporting leg's relevé. Hold the passé-relevé shape 3-5 seconds. Switch.

name: Dance Side Plank with Leg Reach
description: Side plank with top-leg reach — core + hip combination for grand battement and turn stability.
instructions: Side plank on forearm. Lift the top leg as high as possible (battement-style), then lower under control. 8-10 reps per side.

name: Single-Leg Bridge (Dance)
description: Single-leg hip bridge — posterior-chain strength for jumps and takeoffs in dance.
instructions: Lie supine, one foot flat, other leg extended. Drive through the heel, lift hips while keeping pelvis square. Lower with control. 10-12 per side.

name: Dancer's Lateral Lunge with Reach
description: Lateral lunge with torso reach — lateral mobility + rotation for Latin and ballroom dance.
instructions: Stand wide. Shift weight to one side into a lateral lunge while the opposite arm reaches overhead to the lunge side. Reverse smoothly.

name: Hip-Hop Bounce Squat
description: Rhythmic shallow squat bounces — groove endurance for hip-hop dance.
instructions: Stand wide. Bounce through the knees rhythmically, driving hips down-up in a shallow squat pulse. Coordinate with arm swings if desired. 30-60 seconds.

name: Salsa Cross-Step Drill
description: Cross-body rhythmic step with hip action — the foundational Latin footwork drill.
instructions: Stand in a comfortable stance. Step forward with one foot across the body on count 1, replace on 2, step back on 3. Reverse sides on 5-7. Emphasize hip motion on each step.

name: Dance Hip Isolation Drill
description: Isolated hip circles — fundamental salsa/bachata/hip-hop core-rotation drill.
instructions: Stand with a wide stance, knees slightly bent, upper body still. Circle the hips in one direction for 8 reps. Reverse for 8. Progress to figure-8s.

name: Grand Battement (Kick Prep)
description: Ballet-style high kick — hamstring and hip-flexor power for dance.
instructions: Stand with one hand on a wall/barre. Kick the free leg forward as high as possible with a straight knee and pointed foot. Lower with control. 8-10 per direction per side.
cues: kick from the hip, not the back

name: Contemporary Dance Floor Roll
description: Controlled roll from standing to floor and back — contemporary dance floor-work essential.
instructions: From standing, melt down through the spine to the floor one segment at a time, roll across the back, and rise smoothly back to standing using the opposite side.
progression: Add a full tuck roll or tempo shift.

name: Irish Dance Sidestep Drill
description: Rapid lateral tapping footwork on the balls of the feet — Irish dance footwork conditioning.
instructions: Stand tall in a tight posture (arms at sides). On the balls of the feet, rapidly sidestep right-left-right-left, tapping lightly and maintaining an upright chest.

name: Chaînés Turn Prep (Spot Turns)
description: Linked turning prep with spotting — primary turn drill for multiple dance forms.
instructions: Stand with feet together. Step and turn 180° in one direction, snapping the head quickly to maintain a focal spot. Step and turn another 180°. Continue in a line.

name: Dancer Interval Run (Rehearsal Sim)
description: Short-interval aerobic conditioning matched to dance-round timing.
instructions: Run, jump rope, or high-knee in place for 2 minutes at hard pace, then rest 1 minute. Repeat 4-6 rounds.

name: Turnout Clam with External Rotation
description: Deep external hip rotation drill for dancers — targets the six deep rotators.
instructions: Lie on side, knees stacked and bent at 45°. Squeeze heels together; open the top knee like a clam while lifting the top foot. Hold 2 seconds at top, lower with control.

name: Single-Leg Hop (Dance Tempo)
description: Single-leg rhythmic hop — plyometric base for Irish, hip-hop, contemporary.
instructions: Hop on one leg for 10-20 reps in place, emphasizing quiet feet and tempo. Switch legs.

name: Dance Spinal Wave
description: Isolated spinal wave — articulation drill for contemporary, hip-hop, pole.
instructions: Stand wide. Initiate from the tailbone, wave up vertebra by vertebra to the crown of the head. Reverse the wave back down. 6-8 cycles.

name: Frog Stretch (Adductor Opener)
description: Deep adductor stretch — essential mobility drill for dancers, gymnasts, movement athletes.
instructions: On hands and knees, widen the knees as far as comfortable; shins parallel to each other. Lower hips back toward heels until you feel deep adductor stretch. Hold 60-90 seconds.

name: Tai Chi Weight Shift
description: Slow controlled weight transfer between legs — balance and joint-health drill for older practitioners.
instructions: Stand wide. Slowly shift 100% of weight to one leg, lifting the other heel or foot slightly. Hold 2 seconds. Shift fully to the other leg. Move with deliberate slowness.

name: Yoke Walk
description: Loaded yoke carry — strongman signature for full-body stiffness under heavy axial load.
instructions: Step under a loaded yoke with the pad across the upper traps. Brace hard, stand up, walk 40-60 ft with short controlled steps. Set down with control.
home_variation: Barbell in high-bar rack position as substitute.
regression: Barbell back carry at half weight.

name: Tire Flip
description: Large-tire flip — hybrid deadlift-clean-push movement central to strongman and highland games event prep.
instructions: Squat low to the tire with chest against it, hands under the bottom edge. Drive through the legs to lift and rotate, then transition the hands and push the tire over. Walk around and repeat.

name: Sled Push (Heavy)
description: Heavy prowler / sled push — leg-drive strength with near-zero eccentric cost, ideal for strongman and football carryover.
instructions: Set the sled with heavy load. Grip the posts with arms long, body at a strong forward lean. Drive through big powerful steps, full leg extension each stride. Push 30-50 ft. Rest 2-3 min.
home_variation: Push a loaded car in a safe lot.

name: Sled Pull (Backward Drag)
description: Backward sled drag — quad-dominant, knee-friendly conditioning with minimal soreness cost.
instructions: Face the sled with handles or straps. Walk backward, pulling the sled by staying low and driving the heels into the ground on each step. 30-60 feet per effort.
home_variation: Sled with tow strap or heavy tire.

name: Overhead Plate Peasant Carry
description: Single-plate overhead carry — shoulder stability + core endurance under axial load.
instructions: Press a single weight plate overhead with straight arms. Lock out the elbows, ribs stacked over pelvis. Walk 30-50 ft maintaining lockout. Set down, rest, repeat.
regression: Lighter plate or double-DB front rack.

name: Kettlebell Clean-and-Jerk EMOM
description: High-volume kettlebell clean-and-jerk conditioning — kettlebell sport competition staple.
instructions: With a moderate kettlebell in each hand (or one arm at a time), perform clean-and-jerks on the minute, every minute for 5-10 minutes. Start with 4-6 reps per minute; target competition pace (6-10/min).
regression: Short EMOM (3 min) with lighter bell.

name: Belt Squat
description: Loaded squat with load hanging from hips — heavy lower-body work with zero spinal compression.
instructions: Step onto the platform with a loaded belt clipped to hips. Squat to full depth keeping torso upright. Drive through mid-foot to stand. The load hangs below, not on the shoulders.

name: Safety-Bar Squat
description: Back squat with SSB — reduces shoulder ROM demand while loading the posterior chain heavily. Standard powerlifting accessory.
instructions: Unrack the safety bar across the upper back with hands on the padded handles. Brace and squat to depth, driving elbows forward to prevent a chest dump. Stand tall.

name: Snatch Balance
description: Barbell drops into overhead squat from behind-the-neck position — Olympic weightlifting positional drill for receiving the snatch.
instructions: Bar on the back with a wide snatch grip. Dip the knees slightly, drive the bar up while dropping into an overhead squat, catching with locked-out arms in a full squat. Stand with the bar overhead.
home_variation: PVC pipe for technique work at home.
progression: Heavier load or from the drop.

name: Hang Power Clean
description: Clean from the hang position (mid-thigh) caught in a partial squat — builds triple extension without the pull from the floor.
instructions: Set up with feet hip-width, bar at mid-thigh, chest up, shoulders slightly in front of the bar. Drive the hips forward powerfully and shrug, pulling under the bar to catch it on the front rack in a quarter squat. Stand tall.
cues: catch high in the partial squat
progression: Full squat clean from the hang.

name: Wrist Flexion/Extension Mobility
description: Four-way wrist mobility drill — essential for the front rack (clean) and overhead (jerk) positions.
instructions: On all fours, place palms flat under shoulders, fingers forward. Slowly shift weight forward/back to stretch the wrist. Repeat with fingers pointed back, then sideways, then palms-up (backs of hands down).
cues: don't crush — build range over weeks
regression: Shorter hold, less weight through wrist.

name: Foam Roller T-Spine Extension
description: Prone supported thoracic extension over a foam roller — frees the T-spine for the front rack, bench arch, and overhead positions.
instructions: Lie supine with a foam roller across the mid-back (under the shoulder blades). Hands behind the head supporting the neck. Exhale and arch over the roller for 2-3 breaths. Shift the roller up 1 inch, repeat. Cover mid-T-spine only.
cues: stay below the neck and above the ribs
progression: Add light arm load or longer hold.

name: Preacher Curl
description: Biceps isolation with humerus fixed on preacher bench — removes body english and isolates the biceps stretch.
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench, arms draped over the pad, elbows pinned. Hold an EZ-bar or dumbbells with a supinated grip. Curl to full flexion, then lower slowly to near full extension.
cues: full range, don't bounce out of the bottom
home_variation: Standing DB curl against a wall (elbows pinned).

name: Skull Crusher (Lying Triceps Extension)
description: Lying triceps extension — direct triceps stretch and isolation, bodybuilding staple.
instructions: Lie supine on a bench holding an EZ-bar or dumbbells overhead with arms vertical. Keeping elbows fixed, lower the weight toward the forehead (or just past). Extend back to vertical.
cues: lower to forehead then past ears
progression: JM press or heavier skull crusher.

name: Cable Crossover
description: Standing cable chest fly — horizontal adduction with constant tension; bodybuilding chest isolation.
instructions: Stand centered between two high cable pulleys. Grab a handle in each hand with a slight forward lean. Pull hands together in front of the hips in a hugging arc. Squeeze at the bottom; return slowly.
home_variation: Band crossover from a door anchor.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: Side-raise for the lateral deltoid — the signature shoulder isolation lift in bodybuilding.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides, slight forward tilt. Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with the elbows. Pause, lower slowly. Stop before the top-out if the traps take over.
cues: ride the lateral delts — don't swing

name: Bench Arch Thoracic Mobility
description: Thoracic-extension mobility drill on a bench — maintains the bench-press arch without lumbar overload.
instructions: Sit on a bench with feet planted. Slowly arch back, letting the T-spine extend over the edge of the bench. Reach arms overhead. Hold 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply. Sit back up.
cues: extend through the T-spine not the low back

name: Block Pull (Deadlift off Blocks)
description: Deadlift pulled from 2-4 inch blocks — reduces range of motion, allowing heavier supramaximal loading. Powerlifting staple.
instructions: Set the barbell on blocks 2-4 inches off the floor. Set up as for a conventional deadlift from the higher start. Pull with a powerful hip drive, lock out standing tall.
home_variation: Deadlift off plates stacked on the floor.
progression: Deficit deadlift or heavier block pull.

name: Stone-to-Shoulder
description: Atlas stone or heavy sandbag lifted from the ground to shoulder — strongman event-specific lift combining deadlift, clean, and shouldering.
instructions: Straddle the stone/sandbag. Squat and wrap arms around it. Pull it onto the lap, then stand and continue the pull, rolling it up the chest and flipping it onto the shoulder. Alternate shoulders across sets.

name: Adductor Ball Squeeze (Supine)
description: Isometric adductor squeeze — trains the inner-thigh grip used to stay on the horse.
instructions: Lie supine with knees bent, a medicine or pilates ball between the knees. Squeeze the ball hard for 5-10 seconds, breathing throughout. Release partially, repeat.

name: Rider Wall Sit with Ball Squeeze
description: Isometric wall sit with a ball between the knees — mimics the position and inner-thigh demand of the saddle.
instructions: Sit against a wall at 90° knees and 90° hips. Place a ball between the knees and squeeze throughout. Hold for 30-60 seconds. Breathe and maintain posture.
progression: Longer hold or add DB held in front.

name: Kneeling Hip-Flexor Stretch (Long Hold)
description: Long-hold hip-flexor stretch for riders and anyone who sits long hours. Opens the front of the hip.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward (90/90). Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and gently shift hips forward until a stretch is felt in the front hip. Hold 60-90 seconds per side.
progression: Add reach overhead for side-bend stretch.

name: Single-Arm Row + Anti-Rotation Press
description: Alternating single-arm row with anti-rotation Pallof hold — corrects rider asymmetry (stronger rein-hand side).
instructions: In a split stance with a cable or band at chest height, press one hand out while rowing the opposite hand to the ribs. Hold the press briefly, switch. Maintain a tight trunk throughout.
cues: no torso rotation during the hold
home_variation: Resistance band anchored to a door.

name: Hiking Bench Isometric Hold
description: Reclined quad + core isometric mimicking the hiking-out position on a dinghy or keelboat.
instructions: Sit on a bench edge with feet hooked under a stable strap or partner's hands. Lean back 20-30° from vertical, thighs parallel to the ground, torso straight. Hold 30-90 seconds.
cues: straight line from knees to shoulders
progression: Longer hold with weight on chest.

name: PVC Sailing Pull (Bent-Over)
description: Bent-over pull simulating the mainsheet/jib-sheet trim under load. Upper-back endurance for sailors.
instructions: Stand hinged at the hips, a light PVC bar or band looped under one foot. Pull the resistance toward the chest with a rowing motion — mimic the rhythm of trimming a sheet. 15-25 reps per side.
cues: elbows close, drive the shoulder blade back

name: Four-Way Neck Isometric
description: Manual-resistance four-way neck isometric — essential prehab for paragliding, hang-gliding, and grappling.
instructions: Place a palm against the forehead, side of head, and back of head in sequence. Press the head into the hand without moving for 10 seconds each direction. Breathe.

name: Landing Squat Absorption Drill
description: Low-height drop + absorb to a squat — trains the eccentric landing mechanics needed for paragliding/hang-gliding touchdowns.
instructions: Stand on a 6-12" box. Step off (don't jump). Absorb the landing softly into a quarter-squat with bent knees, immediately re-stabilize. Hold the landing for 2 seconds before stepping back up.

name: Thick-Bar (Fat Grip) Hang
description: Dead hang from a thick bar (or Fat Gripz) — grip endurance for sailors, climbers, and spearfishing line-work.
instructions: Attach Fat Gripz or grip a 2"+ thick bar. Hang with arms long, shoulders engaged. Target 20-60 seconds per hang.
home_variation: Towel wrapped around a pull-up bar.

name: Archer Draw Isometric Hold
description: Band-simulated full-draw isometric hold — builds the upper-back endurance specific to archery anchor position.
instructions: Stand tall with a resistance band in the draw hand and the other arm extended toward the imaginary target. Draw the band to the anchor position (side of face/under chin). Hold the full-draw position 15-30 seconds.

name: Scapular Retraction Hold
description: Isometric scapular retraction hold — trains the endurance of the archer's back posture.
instructions: Either prone on a bench or standing with a band pulled apart at chest height. Pull the shoulder blades down and together, hold for 10-15 seconds. Release partially, repeat.

name: Wrist Radial-Ulnar Deviation
description: Lateral wrist movement under light load — prehab for repetitive casting, shooting recoil, and archery wrist alignment.
instructions: Hold a light dumbbell (or hammer) with the forearm supported. Slowly move the wrist side-to-side through a controlled range. 12-15 reps per direction.

name: Shotgun Mount Stability Drill
description: Single-leg shoulder-mount drill — trains the stability required to mount and swing a shotgun consistently in trap/skeet/sporting clays.
instructions: Stand on one leg. With a PVC pipe or unloaded shotgun, practice mounting to the shoulder/cheek weld 8-10 times. Then "swing" through a target arc 5 times. Switch legs.
